title: Whitestone - Search Velocity Hosted API Demo

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-14 11:00am PT | Duration: ~45 mins | Attendees: Maya, Daniel, Ivy (Redwood) — Alex, Priya, Jordan (Whitestone)
---
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, i'll hand it to Daniel for the deep demo in a minute.
00:08 Alex: Great thanks, Maya. we're really looking to improve our site search relevance and speed, so excited to see how your hosted endpoints behave.
00:15 Daniel: Cool. quick agenda: embeddings endpoint, rerank endpoint, show the Console trace and Optimize suggestions, and then we'll talk about security and pilot. sound good?
00:22 Priya: Yep, that works. our SLA target is basically p95 under 100 milliseconds for the search path including rerank, and cost needs to be reasonable, obviously.
00:31 Daniel: Understood. couple quick qualification q's before demo — what's your current embedding vector size and similarity metric? cosine or dot?
00:38 Priya: We're doing 512-d vectors using cosine on a faiss index; queries are short, average seq len ~12 tokens.
00:45 Daniel: Nice, that's pretty standard. you'll probably map straight to redwood-embed-1 or the smaller redwood-embed-lite for lower cost.
00:52 Jordan: Quick question: how does hosted compare to us running our own? Like, are we going to hit network hops that add latency?
00:58 Maya: Good one. hosted avoids you building serving infra and our regional routing keeps requests in-region; we also do caching and prefix KV cache to shave tokens off. if you need zero-egress for compliance, we can discuss Private or Dedicated later.
01:10 Daniel: Ok switching to demo — i'm sharing the console now, can everyone see my screen?
01:15 Priya: Yes.
01:17 Daniel: Cool. First slide is the embeddings endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings with model param. sample payload — here we call redwood-embed-1 and get back a 1024-d vector by default — sorry earlier I said 512 but we have both sizes depending on model.
01:30 Alex: oh, ok — any guidance on tradeoffs? 512 vs 1024?
01:33 Daniel: 512 is cheaper and faster; 1024 gives better semantic fidelity for ambiguous queries. For rerank, often 512 + a strong cross-encoder on top is the sweet spot.
01:45 Daniel: Now the rerank endpoint — this is POST /v1/rerank. you send query, candidate doc ids, embeddings optionally, and the endpoint returns scores and a ranked order. internally it can call a lightweight cross-attention model or use embedding-score heuristics depending on the route config.
01:59 Priya: you mentioned route config — can we pin a policy to force the cross-encoder for certain traffic?
02:06 Daniel: yes, Console routes support per-route model choice and canary policies. you can set a fallback to a cheaper embedding-based reranker if the cross-encoder capacity is saturated.
02:16 Jordan: That fallback bit is interesting — we can't have a bad user experience if the ranker times out. how deterministic is fallback?
02:22 Daniel: it's deterministic by policy: timeout thresholds, regional fallback order, and prioritized model variants. we'll demo a fallback path in the trace.
02:30 Daniel: (screen) here's an example request we run in the console playground — i paste a sample query and ten doc snippets, hit rerank, and you can see latency and token breakdown on the right.
02:40 Maya: note the token-level cost there in the Console, you can see cost per route and per-model so product teams can meter spend.
02:46 Priya: hmm is that real-time? can we export those metrics?
02:49 Ivy: yes, you can export CSV and we have an API for telemetry. retention is configurable as an add-on.
02:55 Alex: let's talk security — we are SOC2 and ISO focused, we also require SSO and SAML, and want KMS for key management.
03:03 Maya: yes, we support SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles in the Console. for key management we integrate with cloud KMS providers and HSM options for Private deployments. SOC2 Type II is available, and we provide audit logs which you can ship to your SIEM.
03:18 Jordan: And data residency? some of our customers must have EU-only storage.
03:22 Maya: we have region pins so you can keep inference and logs in EU regions; for strict residency you can use Private deployment or on-prem package.
03:29 Daniel: back to the demo — i'm going to run a small batch to show server-side batching: 50 queries in a single request. watch the batching efficiency and latency avg.
03:38 Priya: ok got it.
03:40 Daniel: results are in — avg latency 78ms for rerank path with cross-encoder when we used the medium model, note this is with simulated candidate retrieval.
03:48 Alex: that's promising. what's the cost delta when we use the cross-encoder vs pure embedding scoring?
03:52 Daniel: roughly 3–4x higher token compute for cross-encoder per request; but with prefix caching and heuristic filtering you can keep most queries on the embedding-only path and only cross-encode top K where K is small (like 5). Optimize will recommend that split based on your traffic.
04:05 Priya: what's Optimize exactly?
04:07 Daniel: Redwood Optimize is our cost/perf toolkit — it analyzes your traces, suggests batch sizes, quantization (int8), model variants and can propose per-route policies like "embed-only unless top-10 confidence < 0.4". It also shows predicted unit cost savings.
04:22 Alex: do you run Optimize automatically on our traffic? or is it a tool we run?
04:25 Ivy: it's part of the Console — you can run analyses on historical traces and get suggestions, or enable continuous recommendations tied to an alerting policy.
04:33 Daniel: okay next i want to show the traces — here's a request, see span timings: network, model, KV cache lookup, rerank. you can drill into token-level time and see where to optimize.
04:45 Priya: i see a 20ms KV cache hit in some traces — how is that configured?
04:49 Daniel: KV cache is automatic for prefix-heavy queries; you can also configure TTLs and cache sizes per route. it's especially effective for conversational flows but helps search too when query patterns repeat.
04:59 Jordan: about SLAs — do you provide p99 latency guarantees for Hosted?
05:03 Maya: for Hosted API we publish latency profiles and have an SLO. Dedicated capacity comes with contractual SLA for p95/p99 depending on tier. Hosted is performant but for strict contractual p99 you may want Dedicated.
05:15 Alex: ok. timeline — we want to run a pilot for two weeks, can you scope that?
05:20 Maya: yes we'll propose pilot terms: reserved test credits, telemetry sharing, and a small dedicated trial capacity if you want consistent latency.
05:27 Priya: for the pilot we can instrument and send 10k queries and sample docs, run baseline then your suggested config.
05:33 Daniel: perfect — we'll run a baseline embedding-only + top-5 rerank cross-encoder, and an optimized split suggested by Optimize and compare latency/cost.
05:43 Alex: pricing is key — will you share the model unit costs?
05:46 Maya: yes i'll include the pricing sheet with per-model token costs and a sample cost calc for your query volume in the pilot.
05:53 Daniel: small demo note — when we did a local repro we saw tail latency improve by 30% after enabling batching and int8 quantization on the medium cross-encoder. that's a common win.
06:06 Priya: do you support mixed-precision or must quantization be offline?
06:10 Daniel: for Hosted we support quantized variants (int8) that are hosted as model variants — you can route to them. Mixed precision is in the roadmap for Dedicated.
06:19 Alex: curious about monitoring — can we set alerts when rerank confidence drops or when relevance metrics degrade?
06:26 Ivy: yes, you can tie eval sets to the Console, upload prompts and expected ranks, and we will alert on regression thresholds.
06:34 Jordan: can you show sample code for our engineering team — we need a single HTTP example for embeddings + rerank?
06:38 Daniel: sure, i'll paste one in chat; it's also in the repo i will send.
06:41 (short pause, typing)
06:44 Daniel: pasted: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input": "redwood inference" , "model": "redwood-embed-1" }' — returns vector JSON. then call /v1/search or /v1/rerank with the vector and candidate doc ids.
06:56 Priya: are there rate limits for embedding endpoints?
06:59 Maya: yes, there are per-account rate limits but they can be lifted for pilots or Dedicated. we can provide an E2E throughput target in the proposal.
07:07 Alex: any concerns about PII — we index customer product descriptions that may have seller emails. how do you handle that?
07:13 Maya: we support redaction and backfill tooling; plus you can elect not to store requests. for Hosted we have data retention controls and options to disable retention. for stricter needs, Private deployment keeps data in your VPC.
07:24 Priya: ok thanks.
07:26 Daniel: quick demo wrap — i kicked off a sample rerank in the Console and annotated the tokens and scoring reasons. you can export the scoring breakdown for offline analysis.
07:36 Alex: that explainability helps a lot.
07:38 Maya: final -- i'll summarize action items in an email, include the pilot pricing and the benchmark sheet, and daniel will drop the code samples and a short runbook for on-boarding.
07:49 Jordan: favorite — we want to start pilot next week if dates align.
07:52 Maya: great, i'll follow up with proposed kickoff times. thanks everyone.
08:00 End of recording.
---
Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution fuzziness, product names sometimes shortened (e.g., "redwood-embed-1" vs "embed-1"), a few words mis-transcribed (KV -> K V).
